title: CmdPal: ProviderContext contamination between normal and Dock attached palette
author: jiripolasek
summary: Dock-pinned Command Palette commands can receive the normal palette's current page context, such as All Apps, instead of their own provider context.

confidence.rationale: The exact method, contaminated state, and previously proposed focused patch are public and directly match the reproduction.

judgment.rationale: The issue author identifies the exact method and state contamination. A linked PR contains a focused patch but was closed unmerged, so the bug remains an actionable, high-confidence design candidate rather than an existing fix.
evidence: The repro pins Dad Jokes to Dock, navigates normal Command Palette to All Apps, then invokes Dad Jokes and receives All Apps as provider context.
The body names PowerToysAppHostService.GetProviderContextForCommand and its currentContext dependency.
PR 49511 proposed preferring TopLevelViewModel.ProviderContext and explicitly fixed 46401, but it is closed and unmerged.
judgment.recommended_action: Recreate the focused provider-context precedence fix with regression coverage for Dock and normal palette isolation.

fix_assessment.rationale: No active merged fix covers the scoped PowerToys-owned path. The closed PR is concrete evidence for both root cause and minimal remedy, but not an active fix. The dashboard can safely propose a new fork-side design based on provider-context precedence and isolation tests.

proposed_fixes.title: Prefer command provider context over palette page context
proposed_fixes.root_cause: GetProviderContextForCommand uses shared palette currentContext even when a Dock-pinned command has its own TopLevelViewModel.ProviderContext, allowing navigation in one surface to contaminate another.
plan: Resolve context from the command/top-level provider first and use page currentContext only when no command provider context exists.
Keep Dock-attached and normal palette navigation state isolated across command invocation.
Add regression tests for All Apps navigation followed by Dock invocation and for commands that legitimately rely on page fallback context.
verification: Pin Dad Jokes to Dock, navigate the normal palette to All Apps, invoke Dad Jokes, and verify its own provider context.
Repeat across multiple page transitions and confirm normal in-page commands still receive the intended fallback context.

inferences: The command's top-level provider context is the correct primary source, while page currentContext should remain only a fallback for commands without their own provider context.
